Six-layer rhombohedral graphite · line 940, (+⁵) side · 23 November 2026

The tip sets the flat band in line 940

The top-layer flat band of the (+⁵) spectrum in line 940 sits at −32 mV. This report tests whether the tip–sample contact potential alone can put it there, with a neutral stack and no substrate charge, and follows the consequences: the shape of the peak, its dependence on tip distance and apex radius, and why the tip moves the occupied-side features of the spectrum but not the empty-side ones.

  1. One parameter places the flat band. CPot = Wtip − WRG = −0.367 eV puts the peak at −32.4 mV (measured −32.1 mV) without any charge in the stack or the substrate. With WRG ≈ 4.6 eV this is Wtip ≈ 4.23 eV.
  2. The tip makes the peak asymmetric in the measured sense. The ratio of outer to inner half width rises from 0.99 without the tip to 1.09 with it; measured 1.20. The long outer tail of the measured peak is not reproduced.
  3. Tip distance controls the result; apex radius hardly does. At fixed CPot the peak moves from −86 to −20 mV for d = 0.4–1.0 nm, but only from −29 to −34 mV for R = 5–80 nm.
  4. Only the occupied side moves because the field vanishes at V₀ = −CPot/e = +0.37 V. The upper bulk features sit there. Screening by the flat band at EF cuts the top-layer lever arm from 0.22 at negative bias to 0.05 near V₀.
  5. Not explained by the tip: the upper bulk edges (+245 / +355 mV against +272 / +370 mV measured), the 14 mV overshoot of the lower bulk edge, and the outer tail of the flat-band peak.

Hypothesis and model

The top-layer flat band of the (+⁵) spectrum sits at −32 mV in line 940 and at +23 mV in line 514, tens of meV from where a neutral stack puts it (−4 mV). Adsorbates cannot supply that charge: there are too few of them and they are mostly n-alkanes. Tip pulses move the peak slightly. The working assumption is therefore that the tip sets the flat-band position. At the small bias of the flat band, the only field source the tip brings is the contact potential.

Feature positions in mV. Edge rms: root mean square error of the three bulk edges against the measurement. Tail asymmetry: mean dI/dV 40, 60 and 80 mV from the peak on the side away from EF minus that on the side towards it, relative to the peak height.

  • The flat band and the lower bulk edge move together. At the fit the lower edge overshoots: −270 mV against −256 mV.
  • The upper edges stay at +245 / +355 mV for every negative CPot. The measured +272 / +370 mV are out of reach (section 4 explains why).
  • CPot 0 leaves the flat band at −5 mV: the tip at zero contact potential does not gate the top layer near EF.

2 · Shape of the flat-band peak

spectrumpeak (mV)HWHM outer (mV)HWHM inner (mV)outer / innertail asym.
measured−32.123.119.21.200.20
no tip−3.817.417.70.990.01
tip, CPot −0.367 eV−32.419.517.81.090.01

The tip widens the outer flank by 2.1 mV and leaves the inner flank unchanged within 0.2 mV. That covers 49 % of the measured excess of the outer/inner ratio. Mechanism: a level at energy E appears at the bias where eV = E + ΔU₁(V), so its width in bias is its energy width divided by 1 − α, with α = dU₁/d(eV) the local lever arm of the top layer. Across the peak α falls from 0.18 at −75 mV to 0.13 at 0 mV, which stretches the outer flank more than the inner one.

The measured peak also has a long outer tail: 15–20 % of its height remains 100 mV below the peak (tail asymmetry 0.20). The model gives 0.01 at the fit, and at most 0.11 at d 0.4 nm. The tail needs an ingredient the model lacks.

The spectra of the sweeps are stored on a 2.5 mV grid, which quantised the half widths in 2.5 mV steps, the size of the effect. All half widths here come from a re-evaluation on a 0.25 mV grid from the stored potentials, with the half-maximum crossings interpolated.

  • d sets the position. Near d 0.7 nm the flat band moves 8 mV per 0.1 nm. Over R = 5–80 nm it moves by 5 mV: for R ≫ d the field under the apex depends on d and CPot only. The fitted CPot therefore holds only together with d = 0.7 nm; the flat band fixes one combination of the two.
  • The asymmetry grows as the tip approaches, from 1.05 at 1.0 nm to 1.24 at 0.4 nm, which exceeds the measured 1.20, but there the peak sits at −86 mV. At fixed CPot a closer tip both moves the peak away from EF and changes the lever arm, so this sweep does not separate the two. A CPot refit at each d with the peak held at −32 mV does.
  • The upper edges do not move with the geometry (242–245 / 355 mV throughout). The lower edge goes from −300 to −252 mV; the measured −256 mV prefers d ≈ 0.9–1.0 nm, where the flat band is too close to EF.
  • Sweep-grid check: re-solving with 5 mV bias steps from −120 to +20 mV gives d 0.7 nm: peak −32.4 mV (25 mV sweep: −32.4), ratio 1.09 (1.09); d 0.4 nm: peak −86.4 mV (25 mV sweep: −86.4), ratio 1.24 (1.24). The 25 mV sweep grid is converged for the peak position and shape.

4 · Why the tip moves only the occupied-side features

featurebias (mV)V − V₀ (V)ΔU₁ (meV)lever arm αspectral shift (mV)shift at CPot 0
lower bulk edge−270−0.64−790.22−32.5−5
flat band−32−0.40−320.15−28.60
upper bulk edge 1+245−0.12−70.06−2.5+5
upper bulk edge 2+355−0.01−10.050.0+10
  • Electrostatics depends on V + CPot/e only. The CPot −0.367 eV shift curve equals the CPot 0 curve moved by +0.367 V (largest difference 0.02 meV). The tip field vanishes at V₀ = +0.369 V, the bias of zero tip-induced band bending. The upper bulk features at +245 and +355 mV sit 0.12 and 0.01 V below it.
  • Screening depends on where the flat band is. At negative bias the field pushes the flat band below EF; the top layer has no states at EF and the field penetrates (α = 0.22 at −300 mV). Approaching V₀, the flat band returns to EF and its density of states screens (α = 0.06 at +200 mV). A constant α of 0.22 would shift the +245 mV feature by −26 meV; the solve gives −7 meV.
  • Bulk features follow deeper layers. The flat band is a top-layer state and shifts nearly with ΔU₁. The bulk band edges extend through the stack: the lower edge shifts −32.5 mV while ΔU₁ is −79 meV, about the shift of the third layer.
  • CPot 0 shows the contrast. There V₀ = +0.002 V; the field changes sign at zero bias and pushes the features outward on both sides (−5, 0, +5, +10 mV). A shifted occupied side with a fixed empty side is the signature of a negative contact potential of about −0.37 eV.

5 · Open points and next steps

  • Upper bulk edges. The field vanishes there, so no tip setting moves them. Their 15–27 mV deficit belongs to the band structure or the potential profile of the stack.
  • Lower edge and outer tail. The lower edge prefers a weaker tip than the flat band does, and the measured outer tail of the flat band is absent from every tip setting.
  • Separate lever arm from position. Refit CPot at d 0.4, 0.5 and 1.0 nm with the flat band held at −32 mV and compare the half-width ratio and the lower edge.
  • Interlayer ε below 2.6 (noted 22 November): a smaller ε raises the lever arm per unit field.
  • Line 514 (+⁵). Its flat band sits at +23 mV; in this model that needs CPot > 0, i.e. a tip with a larger work function than the sample at the time of that measurement.
  • Experimental test. A tip-height (setpoint) series at one tip state should move the flat band (about 8 mV per 0.1 nm) and the lower edge, and leave the +0.27 and +0.37 V features in place. Features above V₀ ≈ +0.37 V should shift slightly outward.
